target.title: fix(usage): ignore invalid Z.ai reset timestamps
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Z.ai usage fetch converts `nextResetTime` with `new Date(...).getTime()`. Invalid strings produce `NaN`, which is then stored on the usage window as `resetAt` and can poison downstream reset/cooldown logic that expects a finite timestamp or an unset value.

This is provider-contract hardening at the Z.ai usage parser boundary: untrusted quota metadata must not introduce non-finite numbers into domain objects.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts`, keep `resetAt` only when `Number.isFinite(parsedReset)` so invalid reset strings are ignored while valid ISO timestamps still populate `resetAt`.

## User Impact

**Before:** Invalid `nextResetTime` values could yield `resetAt: NaN` on Z.ai usage windows.
**After:** Invalid reset strings leave `resetAt` undefined; valid ISO resets still work.

## Evidence

Branch: `codex/zai-invalid-reset-time` | Base: `upstream/main` | Head: `ed45a4bf` | Node: v24.18.0 — Windows

### Regression tests

``
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > returns HTTP errors for failed requests
 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > returns a stable error for malformed successful usage JSON
 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > returns API message errors for unsuccessful payloads
 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > falls back to a generic API error for blank unsuccessful messages
 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > parses token and monthly windows with reset times
 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > clamps invalid percentages and falls back to alternate plan fields
 ✓ fetchZaiUsage > ignores invalid nextResetTime while preserving valid ISO resets

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
``

- New test proves `nextResetTime: "not-a-date"` yields `resetAt: undefined` while a valid ISO reset still sets `resetAt`.
- Existing Z.ai usage parsing cases remain green.

### Diff summary

``
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.ts       | 4 +++- (finite reset guard)
src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.zai.test.ts  | 42 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ (invalid reset regression)
``

What was not tested: live Z.ai quota API responses; only mocked fetch payloads and a production-function runtime proof.

- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Invalid truthy `nextResetTime` no longer becomes `resetAt: NaN` on Z.ai usage windows; valid ISO resets still populate finite `resetAt`.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, worktree `codex/zai-invalid-reset-time` at `ed45a4bf`; production `fetchZaiUsage` imported from source via `node --import tsx`.
**Steps run after the patch:**
1. Call real `fetchZaiUsage` with a Response whose limits include `nextResetTime: "not-a-date"` and a valid ISO monthly reset.
2. Compare main-style `new Date("not-a-date").getTime()` (NaN) against patched window `resetAt` values.
**Evidence after fix:**

``text
main-style parse: nextResetTime="not-a-date" -> getTime=NaN (Number.isNaN=true)
after fix via fetchZaiUsage:
  Tokens (6h): usedPercent=32, resetAt=<undefined>, resetAtIsFinite=false
  Monthly: usedPercent=12.5, resetAt=1767830400000, resetAtIsFinite=true
``

**Observed result:** Production parser drops the invalid reset and keeps the valid ISO reset as a finite epoch; no `NaN` enters the usage windows.
**Not tested:** Live authenticated Z.ai quota HTTP responses (no live key used); incidence of invalid `nextResetTime` from upstream remains unverified and this change is framed as parser-boundary hardening.
